root_cause_diagnostic: Defect 1 (aso-submission-parts.yml:build): the workflow's 'Commit to main' step hand-rolled `git commit` + a `git pull --rebase` retry loop -- the exact shape test_no_hand_rolled_publish.py documents as having silently failed to publish on three prior lanes. Confirmed reproducing on current HEAD via `pytest -k aso-submission-parts` before any fix.

Defect 2 (blind claim-coverage witness): claim_coverage.py credited 'The cut of 5.0 is adopted as a convention.' to the pattern `cut of \d|threshold`, which matches any single digit -- so PREFLIGHT_FULL's full (unsampled) ablation found the witness stayed green after perturbing the digit (5->7), the same class of defect claim_coverage.ABLATION_BLOCKED_BY_A_KNOWN_FALSE_POSITIVE already documents for a different manuscript's `HTTP \d{3}`.

CI infra defect 1 (lost diagnostic): GitHub Actions runs every `run:` step under `bash -e` by default; `set -uo pipefail` only adds flags, it does not clear `-e`. The first preflight-full-record.yml dispatch (run 33101598851) aborted the instant preflight.sh returned nonzero, before the EXIT= marker or any log content was written, so the 'Record evidence' and 'Publish' steps both read `skipped` and nothing about WHY survived anywhere.

CI infra defect 2 (missing uv): the second dispatch (run 33104631542), after fixing defect 1, surfaced the real preflight result: 53 modalities test failures, every one ModuleNotFoundError-shaped, and preflight.sh's own log said so verbatim. Root-caused by reading scripts/dev-setup.sh directly: it installs everything the gates need EXCEPT `uv` itself, and a vanilla ubuntu-latest runner does not carry it. The workflow's fallback line (copied from aso-submission-parts.yml, which never runs the modalities suite) silenced dev-setup.sh's own failure instead of fixing it.

Also moved the workflow_dispatch `reason` input out of direct `${{ }}` interpolation into `env:` (script-injection hardening, matching aso-offtarget.yml's existing convention). Verified: test_no_hand_rolled_publish.py 56/56 (was 55/56); ran successfully in production shortly after (commit df2bc4b, 'ASO submission parts rebuilt on a runner (CI)').

research/manuscripts/tests/test_the_paper_states_what_its_own_claims_depend_on.py: added test_the_falsification_cut_is_the_stated_value(), a narrow witness pinned to the exact value (`cut of 5\.0`), deliberately separate from the existing wide presence check (which stays wide on purpose -- absence detection). .github/workflows/preflight-full-record.yml (new): a reusable workflow_dispatch(sha) that checks out the exact commit, runs PREFLIGHT_FULL=1, calls record_bar_evidence.py, and publishes the receipt+log to main through the one commit primitive -- always (if: always()), so a red run's diagnostic still lands rather than being lost. Fixed twice in production (bash -e trap, then uv provisioning) before its third dispatch succeeded end-to-end.
redirect.class_of_defect: The two ASO defects are each an existing, named class this repository already tracks (hand-rolled-publish, blind-witness) recurring on a new instance; not swept for further instances of either this cycle. The CI infra defects are new -- the first CI workflow this repository has that runs the FULL preflight tier on a fresh runner, so both were first-instance discoveries rather than recurrences. The AUT-PD-013 collision is itself an instance of a named class this repository already tracks (AUT-PROP-013: ids and claims minted from committed state collide when two sessions act concurrently on the same state) -- this cycle skipped claiming a small follow-on item before starting on it, which is exactly the omission that class exists to name.
